groups.name: Tofino and Ucluelet
groups.intro: Tofino and Ucluelet share one stretch of coast: Tofino for long beaches and surf, Ucluelet for a quieter harbour town and rugged shoreline.

trips.title: Two days on the west coast
trips.summary: Beach, rainforest and a sunset cove in Tofino, then the Wild Pacific Trail, lighthouse and harbour in Ucluelet.
trips.season: Every season works. Summer is busiest, spring and fall are quieter, winter is for storm watching.

stops.name: Chesterman Beach
stops.what: A 2.7-kilometre stretch of white sand shaped like a W. Walk it, or take a beginner surf lesson on the sandy bottom.

stops.name: Rainforest Trail
stops.what: Two boardwalk loops through the old-growth forest of Pacific Rim National Park Reserve, right off the Pacific Rim Highway.

stops.name: Tonquin Beach
stops.what: A sunset-facing cove reached by an 800-metre gravel path with viewing platforms. Calmer water than the surf beaches.

stops.name: Wild Pacific Trail, Lighthouse Loop
stops.what: The 2.6-kilometre Lighthouse Loop takes about 45 minutes along black volcanic rock and leads to Amphitrite Point Lighthouse.

stops.name: Ancient Cedars Loop
stops.what: Passes two red cedars estimated to be over 800 years old. The nearby Rocky Bluffs are a whale watching vantage point in migration season.

stops.name: Ucluelet Aquarium
stops.what: A catch-and-release aquarium at the foot of Main Street with touch tanks. Fully indoor and seasonal, typically March through early December.

stops.name: Ucluelet Harbour Walk
stops.what: Boardwalks through the inner boat basin, with fishing vessels, herons, bald eagles and the occasional sea otter.

trips.source: Tofino; Tofino - Surfing; Ucluelet; Best Time to Stay in Ucluelet or Tofino_ Weather, Prices, and What to See

trips.title: Four days on the west coast
trips.summary: Tofino's beaches, a day on Clayoquot Sound, then Ucluelet's coast, bog boardwalk, harbour and a paddle.
trips.season: Every season works. Summer is busiest, spring and fall are quieter, winter is for storm watching.

stops.name: Long Beach
stops.what: Part of the Long Beach Unit of Pacific Rim National Park Reserve, between Tofino and Ucluelet. A Parks Canada pass is required.

stops.name: Chesterman Beach
stops.what: A 2.7-kilometre stretch of white sand shaped like a W. Walk it, or take a beginner surf lesson on the sandy bottom.

stops.name: Tonquin Beach
stops.what: A sunset-facing cove reached by an 800-metre gravel path with viewing platforms. Calmer water than the surf beaches.

stops.name: Hot Springs Cove
stops.what: Reached only by water or air from Tofino: a 2-kilometre cedar boardwalk to five natural pools. A typical excursion lasts 6 to 7 hours.

stops.name: Whale and wildlife tour (shorter option)
stops.what: Many tours last about two to three hours. Main whale watching season is March through November, with gray whales in spring.

stops.name: Wild Pacific Trail, Lighthouse Loop
stops.what: The 2.6-kilometre Lighthouse Loop takes about 45 minutes along black volcanic rock and leads to Amphitrite Point Lighthouse.

stops.name: Amphitrite Point Lighthouse
stops.what: An active beacon on the southern tip of the peninsula, good for spotting migrating whales in spring and sea lions on the offshore rocks.

stops.name: Ucluelet Aquarium
stops.what: A catch-and-release aquarium at the foot of Main Street with touch tanks. Fully indoor and seasonal, typically March through early December.

stops.name: Ucluelet Inlet paddle
stops.what: The sheltered harbour suits beginners and a calm morning paddle past fishing docks, with bald eagles and kingfishers along the shore.

stops.name: Shorepine Bog Trail
stops.what: An 800-metre boardwalk loop through a stunted forest in the national park. Stay on the boardwalk to protect the slow-growing plants.

stops.name: Whiskey Dock and Ucluelet Harbour Walk
stops.what: A historic pier with one of the best views of the harbour, next to boardwalks through the working boat basin.

trips.source: Tofino; Tofino - Surfing; Ucluelet; Best Time to Stay in Ucluelet or Tofino_ Weather, Prices, and What to See

trips.title: Two days at the Pacific Rim Whale Festival
trips.summary: The festival guide's own one-day plan followed by its weekend list: whale spotting, a tour, food, a talk and a coastal hike.
trips.season: March. 2026 festival dates are March 14 to 21, and 2027 dates are March 13 to 20.

stops.name: Morning whale spotting or beach walk
stops.what: Learn to look for blows, dark backs and flukes. Bring binoculars, warm layers and patience, as sightings are never guaranteed.

stops.name: Midday festival event or market
stops.what: Look for the Parade of Whales and Wonders, which opens the week, or the Chowder Chowdown, where local restaurants and chefs showcase coastal chowder.

stops.name: Afternoon Wild Pacific Trail or Long Beach
stops.what: Coastal walks in Ucluelet or the national park. Dress for cool, wet, windy March conditions.

stops.name: Dinner in Ucluelet or Tofino
stops.what: Support local restaurants. Choose a mix of outdoor and indoor events in case the weather changes.

stops.name: Whale watching tour
stops.what: Spring tours focus on the gray whale migration, from Barkley Sound or Clayoquot Sound. Reserve ahead, as tours and lodging are in demand.

stops.name: Food or art event
stops.what: The festival mixes free and ticketed events, including food, art, markets and family activities. Check ticket details first.

stops.name: Speaker or education event
stops.what: Talks, workshops and education sessions on whales, marine mammals and coastal ecosystems. Some are free, others need registration.

stops.name: Coastal hike
stops.what: Walk the Wild Pacific Trail or take a rainforest walk, and leave time to drive between the towns and the national park.

groups.name: Whistler
groups.intro: Whistler is a mountain resort that works in every season, with a walkable village at the base.

trips.title: Two days in Whistler
trips.summary: A classic first day in the village and on the gondola, then an outdoor adventure day chosen by season.
trips.season: Winter (December to February) for snow; summer (June to August) for biking and lakes; fall is quieter.

stops.name: Whistler Village
stops.what: The heart of the resort: walkable, with shops, restaurants, cafes, bars and lift bases, and easy to enjoy without a car.

stops.name: Peak 2 Peak Gondola
stops.what: Connects Whistler and Blackcomb mountains with big alpine views. Mountain temperatures are often 5 to 10°C cooler than the village, so dress in layers.

stops.name: Squamish Lil'wat Cultural Centre
stops.what: Shares the living cultures, stories, art and traditions of the Squamish Nation and Lil'wat Nation. A good rainy-day stop and a strong choice for families.

stops.name: Dinner in the village
stops.what: Patios and mountain views in summer, a cozy and festive village in winter.

stops.name: Winter: ski, snowboard, snowshoe or cross-country ski
stops.what: Whistler Blackcomb has two mountains, ski schools and rentals. Lost Lake is a convenient area for Nordic skiing and snowshoeing.

stops.name: Summer: bike, hike, paddle, zipline or lake day
stops.what: Whistler Mountain Bike Park offers lift-access downhill riding. Alpine trails, lakes and ziplines round out the summer choices.

stops.name: Scandinave Spa or a good meal
stops.what: Outdoor hot baths, cold plunges, steam rooms and saunas in a forest setting. Quiet and phone-free.

trips.source: Top Things to See and Do in Whistler

trips.title: Three days in Whistler
trips.summary: Village and mountain views, one big activity day of your choice, then a slow day of lake, culture and spa.
trips.season: Winter (December to February) for snow; summer (June to August) for biking and lakes; fall is quieter.

stops.name: Arrive in Whistler
stops.what: Staying near the village gives the easiest access to restaurants, shops, lifts and tours.

stops.name: Explore the village
stops.what: The heart of the resort: walkable, with shops, restaurants, cafes, bars and lift bases, and easy to enjoy without a car.

stops.name: Peak 2 Peak Gondola
stops.what: Connects Whistler and Blackcomb mountains with big alpine views. Mountain temperatures are often 5 to 10°C cooler than the village, so dress in layers.

stops.name: A relaxed dinner
stops.what: Choose a patio or a village restaurant and keep the evening easy.

stops.name: Ski or snowboard
stops.what: Whistler Blackcomb is known as North America's largest ski resort, with runs from beginner slopes to advanced bowls. Winter is busy, so book early.

stops.name: Mountain bike
stops.what: Whistler Mountain Bike Park is famous for lift-access downhill, flow trails and jump lines. Start with lessons if you are new.

stops.name: Alpine hike
stops.what: Alpine trails reached by gondola, with wildflowers, viewpoints and lakes in summer and early fall. Bring layers and proper footwear.

stops.name: Zipline
stops.what: Adventure tours are easy to book, especially in summer. Check age, height, weight and weather rules before booking.

stops.name: Rafting or adventure tour
stops.what: Rafting, ATV, off-road and other tours suit groups, families with older kids and first-time visitors who do not have their own gear.

stops.name: Lost Lake
stops.what: Close to the village but peaceful and forested. Swim, picnic, walk, bike or paddle in summer; snowshoe or cross-country ski in winter.

stops.name: Valley Trail
stops.what: A paved path system connecting neighbourhoods, lakes, parks, viewpoints and the village. Walk, bike or run without driving.

stops.name: Audain Art Museum or Squamish Lil'wat Cultural Centre
stops.what: Art from British Columbia, including important Indigenous art and works by major regional artists. Good for rainy days and slower afternoons.

stops.name: Scandinave Spa
stops.what: Outdoor hot baths, cold plunges, steam rooms and saunas in a forest setting. Quiet and phone-free.

stops.name: A final village meal
stops.what: End the trip with dinner in the village.

trips.source: Top Things to See and Do in Whistler

groups.name: Squamish
groups.intro: Squamish sits where the mountains meet Howe Sound, with big views, waterfalls and rugged outdoor adventure close to town.

trips.title: Two days in Squamish
trips.summary: Views and waterfalls on day one, then one or two outdoor adventures of your choice on day two.
trips.season: Year-round. Add Brackendale eagle watching in winter, best from late fall into winter.

stops.name: Shannon Falls
stops.what: A tall waterfall dropping down granite cliffs after a short, easy walk from the parking area, beside Stawamus Chief Provincial Park.

stops.name: Sea to Sky Gondola
stops.what: Rides up for views over Howe Sound, Shannon Falls and the Stawamus Chief, with easy trails, lookout platforms and a summit lodge at the top.

stops.name: Sky Pilot Suspension Bridge
stops.what: At the top of the Sea to Sky Gondola, with mountain and Howe Sound views. A gondola ticket is needed; go early for fewer people.

stops.name: Howe Sound viewpoints
stops.what: Squamish sits where mountains meet the ocean. Enjoy the sound from the gondola, the Chief, highway viewpoints and waterfront areas.

stops.name: Downtown cafes or breweries
stops.what: A growing food, coffee and craft beer scene. Stop for coffee, visit a brewery or browse the shops.

plan.title: Day 2: Outdoor Adventure (choose one or two)

stops.name: Hike the Stawamus Chief
stops.what: Squamish's most famous landmark. The hike is steep and challenging, with stairs, rocks, roots and three peaks; the First Peak is the shortest summit.

stops.name: Go mountain biking
stops.what: One of Canada's best mountain biking destinations, with forest trails, technical terrain and flow trails. Book a lesson or guided ride if new.

stops.name: Alice Lake Provincial Park
stops.what: Lakes, forest, walking trails, picnic areas and swimming in season. Nature without a hard climb; arrive early on warm summer days.

stops.name: Smoke Bluffs Park
stops.what: Best known for rock climbing, with short walks, forest trails and small viewpoints close to town.

stops.name: Squamish Estuary
stops.what: Where river, marsh, mountain and ocean meet. Good for easy walks, birdwatching and quiet views.

stops.name: Railway Museum of British Columbia
stops.what: British Columbia's railway history and heritage, with train equipment and exhibits in a mountainside setting.

stops.name: Winter option: Brackendale eagle watching
stops.what: Bald eagles gather around the Squamish River during the salmon run. Bring binoculars and keep a respectful distance.

trips.source: Top 15 Things to See and Do in Squamish

groups.name: Squamish and Whistler
groups.intro: Squamish and Whistler sit on the same Sea to Sky Highway, so a rugged-to-resort trip pairs naturally.

trips.title: Two days from Squamish to Whistler
trips.summary: Waterfall, gondola and downtown Squamish on day one, then village, gondola, lake and culture in Whistler.
trips.season: Both are great in summer. Whistler is best in winter for snow; Squamish is a quieter winter stop.

stops.name: Dinner in the village
stops.what: A village meal to finish the trip.

trips.summary: Squamish views, a Squamish adventure day, then a Whistler resort day with gondola, lake, shopping and spa.
trips.season: Both are great in summer. Whistler is best in winter for snow; Squamish is a quieter winter stop.

stops.name: Drive to Whistler in the evening

stops.name: Village shopping
stops.what: Wander between shops, galleries, gear stores and cafes in the walkable village.

stops.name: Spa, dinner or nightlife
stops.what: Outdoor hot baths, cold plunges, steam rooms and saunas in a forest setting. Quiet and phone-free.

groups.name: Vancouver Island south
groups.intro: Victoria, Sooke and Sidney sit at the southern tip of Vancouver Island: harbour landmarks, wild coast and a booktown on the Saanich Peninsula.

trips.title: Three days on southern Vancouver Island
trips.summary: Victoria's harbour and museum, Sooke's river pools and beaches, then Butchart Gardens and the Sidney waterfront.

stops.name: Inner Harbour
stops.what: The heart of Victoria, framed by the Neo-baroque Parliament Buildings and the Fairmont Empress Hotel.

stops.name: BC Parliament Buildings
stops.what: Victoria's premier architectural landmark: a grand Neo-baroque complex with a copper dome, on the Inner Harbour.

stops.name: Royal BC Museum
stops.what: Walk through a replica 19th-century town, stand beneath a towering woolly mammoth and explore Indigenous cultures. Across from the Parliament Buildings.

stops.name: Fisherman's Wharf
stops.what: Colourful houseboats, fresh seafood kiosks and working fishing vessels in a living neighbourhood on the water.

stops.name: Sooke Potholes Provincial Park
stops.what: Deep, smooth rock pools on the Sooke River, carved from volcanic rock by boulders in swirling currents.

stops.name: Whiffin Spit
stops.what: A 1.5-kilometre gravel bar into Sooke Harbour: a quick coastal walk with mountain and water views.

stops.name: French Beach Provincial Park
stops.what: A long pebble-and-sand beach on the Juan de Fuca Strait, about 20 kilometres west of Sooke, popular with families.

plan.title: Day 3: Sidney and the Saanich Peninsula

stops.name: The Butchart Gardens
stops.what: A 55-acre garden grown from a former limestone quarry, a National Historic Site of Canada transformed by Jennie Butchart from 1904.

stops.name: Sidney Waterfront
stops.what: A flat, barrier-free 2.5-kilometre paved walkway with public art and views of the Gulf Islands and Mount Baker.

stops.name: Beacon Avenue
stops.what: Canada's only Booktown, with independent shops and cafes along a tree-lined avenue sloping down to the Salish Sea.

stops.name: China Beach
stops.what: A fine-sand beach in Juan de Fuca Provincial Park, roughly 35 kilometres west of Sooke and a trailhead for the Juan de Fuca Marine Trail.

stops.name: Quadra Island
stops.what: A 10-minute ferry ride from downtown: the largest Discovery Island, known for artists, hidden beaches and deep Indigenous history. Worth a full day.

stops.name: Ripple Rock Trail
stops.what: An 8-kilometre return trail to a high cliff over Seymour Narrows, where the water moves as fast as a river.

stops.name: Cathedral Grove
stops.what: Giant Douglas firs over 800 years old, on Highway 4 between Qualicum and Port Alberni.

stops.name: Chesterman Beach
stops.what: A 2.7-kilometre stretch of white sand shaped like a W. Walk it, or take a beginner surf lesson on the sandy bottom.

stops.name: Tonquin Beach
stops.what: A sunset-facing cove reached by an 800-metre gravel path with viewing platforms. Calmer water than the surf beaches.

stops.name: Hot Springs Cove
stops.what: Reached only by water or air from Tofino: a 2-kilometre cedar boardwalk to five natural pools. A typical excursion lasts 6 to 7 hours.

stops.name: Wild Pacific Trail, Lighthouse Loop
stops.what: The 2.6-kilometre Lighthouse Loop takes about 45 minutes along black volcanic rock and leads to Amphitrite Point Lighthouse.

stops.name: Amphitrite Point Lighthouse
stops.what: An active beacon on the southern tip of the peninsula, good for spotting migrating whales in spring and sea lions on the offshore rocks.

stops.name: Ucluelet Aquarium
stops.what: A catch-and-release aquarium at the foot of Main Street with touch tanks. Fully indoor and seasonal, typically March through early December.

trips.source: Victoria - Agent Trek; Chemainus; Nanaimo; The Parksville and Qualicum; Campbell River; Tofino; Ucluelet

groups.name: Vancouver Island mountain biking
groups.intro: Vancouver Island is a biking road trip: pedal-access trail riding in a string of trail towns, each with its own style.

trips.title: Three days of Vancouver Island mountain biking
trips.summary: One day each in Nanaimo, Cumberland and Cowichan: technical trails, classic Island singletrack, and flow or downhill-style riding.
trips.season: Spring through fall. Fall is one of the best seasons, and spring dirt can be very good but wet.

stops.name: Nanaimo
stops.what: Technical riding with rocky sections, roots, climbs and ridgelines across several zones, including Doumont, Westwood, South Benson and Extension Ridge.

stops.name: Cumberland and Comox Valley
stops.what: Often considered the heart of Vancouver Island mountain biking: forest singletrack, loam, flow trails and technical descents beside a bike-town village.

stops.name: Cowichan Valley
stops.what: A region of several riding zones: Cobble Hill for easier riding, Mount Tzouhalem for variety, Maple Mountain for technical forest and Mount Prevost for advanced downhill.

trips.source: Vancouver Island_ Best Mountain Biking Spots

trips.title: Five days of Vancouver Island mountain biking
trips.summary: Start in Victoria, ride Cowichan and Nanaimo, spend time in Parksville or Hammerfest, then finish in Cumberland.

trips.season: Spring through fall. Fall is one of the best seasons, and spring dirt can be very good but wet.
